content.text:
Done and pushed to `main`. Dev server is running at localhost:3000 if you want to look.

**What changed**

Picking a country still slides the globe left and shows the timeline. Now, selecting a period is a separate beat from entering the story:

1. Scroll/click a period in the drum → globe slides further left (`-58vw`, slightly shrunk) and the era's 3D figure fades in on the space it vacated, with the era name and note under it.
2. Choose that same period again (click the centered row, or Enter) → the existing fade-out into `/story/[code]/period/[periodId]`.

If you click the already-selected top row before any figure has appeared, that first activation summons the figure rather than navigating — so the reveal can't be skipped by accident.

The figure auto-turns slowly, and you can drag to spin it; a flick keeps gliding and settles back into the idle turn.

**Your model**

`raw/model.glb` → [frontend/public/spain/models/pre-roman-iberia.glb](frontend/public/spain/models/pre-roman-iberia.glb). I renamed it to the period id because that's the lookup convention — for the rest, just drop files as:

```
frontend/public/<country>/models/<period-id>.<glb|gltf|fbx|obj>
```

e.g. `frontend/public/spain/models/al-andalus.glb`. The extension is probed at runtime (verified: existing file 200s, missing one 404s and falls through), so **glTF, FBX and OBJ all work with no code change** — that covers the "not sure of the format" part. Period ids are in [lib/spain-periods.ts](frontend/lib/spain-periods.ts). Any model is auto-centered and scaled to a fixed height, so a 200-unit FBX and a 1.8-unit GLB read the same on screen; if one needs nudging there's a `figureTuning` map in [lib/period-figures.ts](frontend/lib/period-figures.ts#L33) for per-model `scale`/`rotationY`, and `figureOverrides` for filenames that can't follow the convention.

Eras with no model yet get a stylised gold placeholder figure, so the whole transition is testable now — scroll past Pre-Roman Iberia and you'll see it.

One thing worth flagging: I deleted [frontend/three.d.ts](frontend/three.d.ts). It contained `declare module "three"`, which — because `baseUrl` is `.` — was shadowing the installed `@types/three` and typing all of three.js as `any`. Removing it gives real types; `tsc --noEmit`, `next lint` and `next build` all pass.

Not done: the figure is hidden below the `md` breakpoint, since on mobile the timeline already takes the full width and there's nowhere to stage it.
